build_contract: Same LLVM22.1.8 O2 jemalloc; only R35 native compiler change
fixture: Same frozen 1.33m/14d RAW_UUID build-coherent TimeSeries table as R35-native-1330k-local-20261104.json
query: avg by(stage)(avg_over_time(ci_duration[1d])) through native prometheusQueryRange over14 daily evaluation timestamps
protocol: Fresh server stock/candidate/candidate/stock. Each phase has one warmup wave and two measured waves. Each wave starts two requests through a barrier and waits for both responses. All attempted requests, including memory failures, retained. No other local benchmark ran concurrently.
correctness: All successful outputs have532 label/timestamp/value points equal within1e-10 to the complete independently validated large-fixture oracle. Exact user part census unchanged. Terminal query_log records present for all24 attempted requests.

stock.failure_type: Total server memory limit, OvercommitTracker stops one query. This is not a kernel OOM kill.
stock.representative_error: (total) memory limit exceeded: would use2.66GiB, current RSS2.65GiB, maximum2.65GiB. Query selected to stop by OvercommitTracker. While executing AggregatingTransform.
stock.phase_result: Exactly one success and one memory error in each of all six waves, including warmups.

candidate.phase_result: Both requests succeed in each of all six waves, including warmups.

interpretation: At this exact resource cap and workload, eliminating the redundant aggregation increases observed safe concurrency from one broad request to two. The experiment does not establish a general concurrency limit, production error rate or p95/p99. Do not compute a speedup after silently discarding the stock memory failures.
next_gate: Longer open-loop mixed-selector load, concurrent ingestion/merges, wider label counts and retention, and tenant/ACL verification before production promotion.
